sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains why the manna is specifically described as "raining down," emphasizing that despite its lofty source as dew, it descended into physicality to teach that life comes not from bread alone but from the utterance of Hashem.

translations.translation: And to understand the specific expression "I will rain down,"
"I will rain down for you bread from heaven,"
behold, this will be understood from what is explained in Likkutei Torah in the discourses of Parshat Eikev49,
that although in general the manna is the aspect of dew
(as above),
nevertheless it became materialized to the extent that they ground it in a mortar and cooked it in a pot50,
and even regarding the righteous, for whom the eating of the manna was without effort,
nevertheless they had to "gather it from upon the opening of the tent"51,
and afterward the eating itself had to be in its simple sense,
and it is even explained in the early authorities52
that there was also the matter of the blessing "Who brings forth bread from the heavens" or in another formulation, etc.52.
But nevertheless,
through their seeing and eating the manna, whose root is from the dew of the precious stones,
and it was drawn downward until it became materialized
[as explained in the discourses of the Alter Rebbe from the year 5568 (1808) and elsewhere53],
through this it would become known to them that "not on bread alone does man live"54,
meaning
(not that there is no need for the matter of eating bread,
but rather that there must be eating
(which is why the manna became materialized),
however)
the negation is that it is not on bread alone,
that is, the aspect of the Immanent Presence that is in this
(as explained above),
but rather "on every utterance of the mouth of Hashem does man live,"
through the utterance of the mouth of Hashem being clothed in the bread,
just as the manna became materialized, etc.
And as it is written of the Torah that "it is hidden from the eyes of all living"55,
"and I was a delight before Him"56,
and from there it traveled and descended in the secret of the chain of descent from level to level etc. until it became clothed etc. in ink upon the scroll57,
in the letters of the Torah58.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the manna brought a new level of awareness, teaching that even in eating physical bread, one must know with complete certainty that life comes from the utterance of Hashem.

translations.translation: And this is the general concept of "I will rain down for you bread from heaven,"
for although Israel were beforehand at the height of levels,
nevertheless,
when "I will rain down for you bread from heaven," their previous level does not reach the level that must be attained by them through this matter.
Regarding the study of Torah,
that it must be in a manner of walking,
"walk in My Torah"
(specifically "Mine," analogous to the distinction between "the commandments of Hashem" and "My commandments"59),
and particularly according to what is explained in Torah Or60
that in the "walking" of this verse
("walk in My Torah")
there are two aspects: from above downward and from below upward,
and regarding the service of "all your deeds shall be for the sake of Heaven" and "in all your ways know Him"61,
that all of a person's needs are called by the name "eating"62,
behold, through the manna it is effected that although one knows that regarding this bread there is a possibility to say that on it alone does man live,
for the intention is for this bread as it is in its ultimate perfection
(as explained above),
nevertheless, this is only bread from the earth,
and "not on bread alone does man live, for on every utterance of the mouth of Hashem does man live."
And in this itself, "in order to make known to you" specifically,
meaning that this is not only in a manner of faith,
but rather knowledge, and in the ultimate perfection of knowledge,
that one knows at the time of eating the bread that he then receives vitality from the utterance of the mouth of Hashem, through which man lives.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the eternal nature of the manna's lesson, showing that even in times of limited service, one must incorporate the inner dimension of Torah and the aspect of "One" to sustain all levels of divine service.

translations.translation: And behold, the Torah is eternal18,
and seemingly there is room to inquire: what is the eternality of all the details and of the general concept of "I will rain down for you bread from heaven"?
There is further room to inquire:
For it is stated in Berachot63
"Moshe instituted for Israel the blessing of 'Who sustains' at the time that the manna descended for them"
(therefore we say "Who sustains" in the third person64)
"Yehoshua instituted for them the blessing of the land"
("on the land and on the sustenance,"
the land that produces sustenance65),
and we are obligated even now,
that the first blessing of Grace After Meals is the blessing of "Who sustains," which is for the manna.
And the concept is as explained above66
at length,
that even when the service is
(for whatever reason)
only in the aspect of the Lower Unity,
nevertheless, from time to time they need also an illumination from the aspect of the Upper Unity67,
to the extent that this will effect a revelation.
And similarly, when the service is only in the manner of subjugation,
nevertheless, there must be contemplation, at least in comprehension, also in the matter of transformation.
And similarly regarding the study of Torah,
that although the main study is seemingly in the revealed aspect of Torah,
where there is the matter of toil,
nevertheless, there must also be the matter of the inner dimension of Torah68,
as explained at length in the Kuntres Etz HaChayim69
and in several discourses.
And on the contrary,
the matter of the inner dimension of Torah is the matter of salt, through which all study is sustained.
As it is stated in Shabbat70
"A parable of a person who said to his agent, 'Bring me up a kor of wheat to the attic'"
[meaning the matter of wheat as it is in a lofty manner]
"... 'Did you mix in a kav of salt?' He said to him, 'No'...",
meaning that without the matter of salt71,
there is no sustenance even for a kor of wheat in the attic.
And similarly regarding the general service of the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,
for our sages said that it must be "Just as there is in Your heart only One, so too there is in our heart only One"72,
meaning that they must remember that "there is in Your heart"
(of Yaakov,
Atzilut)
"only One,"
and this effects that "there is in our heart"
(the tribes,
Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah)
"only One, just as there is in Your heart..."
And this means that in addition to there being the aspect of "and,"
there is also for it the aspect of "One."
For although the aspect of "and" is the extension of the kingship of the Holy One, blessed be He, throughout all the worlds,
nevertheless, this does not reach the aspect of "One,"
for even though "and" in letter substitution is "One"73,
behold, this does not reach the letters as they are before the substitution,
as understood from what is explained in Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmunah74
regarding the matter of substitutions, etc.
